clue.text: Skill of journalists covering centre of town

indicators.note: the journalists' word wraps around the other piece, covering it

parts.note: the press is the collective name for journalists

indicators.note: the centre of the four-letter word town is its two middle letters

explanation.surface: A reporter's talent for covering events in the middle of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' reads like reporting on a story, but it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Prowess is great ability or expertise, a close synonym of skill.

clue.text: Nude lying in grass must be rejected

indicators.note: the nude word is lying inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
in the buff means naked, so buff can stand for nude

explanation.surface: A naked sunbather in the long grass is turned away.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuff is to snub or turn down, so rebuffed means rejected.

clue.text: Did the dishes, exhausted

definitions.meaning: cleaned the plates and cutlery after a meal
finished, spent, having no more to give

explanation.surface: Someone who has done the washing-up and is now worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both cleaned crockery and, figuratively, finished or no longer successful.

clue.text: Stoppage pays for work on the land

parts.note: to stand a drink is to pay for it, so stands means pays for
to till is to plough and cultivate soil

explanation.surface: A halt in farming that has to be paid for.
explanation.definitionFit: A standstill is a halt where all movement or activity has ceased.

clue.text: Excellent answer after lifting diamond, say

indicators.note: the answer's letter comes after the other piece
in a down clue lifting the word turns it upside down, reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: a diamond is an example of a gem

explanation.surface: A superb reply after someone hoists up a precious stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns GEM upward in this down clue to give MEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is slang for great or terrific, an informal synonym of excellent.

clue.text: Put phone down on copper needing time away

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
off means away, as in going off

explanation.surface: Hanging up on a police officer who needs some time off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but gives the chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone off is to end a call abruptly, as by hanging up on them.

clue.text: Angry leaver may sup hot port

indicators.note: to sup is to take in a drink, so leaver takes the hot letter inside
angry suggests the letters are stirred up and agitated

parts.note: H is the letter on a hot tap

explanation.surface: A furious person leaving might sip something hot, or a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angry' mixes LEAVER plus H, which 'may sup' takes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Havre is a major French seaport at the mouth of the Seine.

clue.text: Promised to be busy

definitions.meaning: occupied, as a phone line or toilet is

explanation.surface: Having made a pledge commits one to being occupied.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaged means both betrothed and occupied, as a telephone line can be.

clue.text: May must accept European sovereignty, being blue

indicators.note: the word for may takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: may and can both express permission or ability
rule is power or authority over a state

explanation.surface: A political jibe at Prime Minister May bowing to European control and feeling down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like Theresa May, the Prime Minister of the day, but it is the verb of permission.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerulean is a deep sky-blue colour, so it names a shade of blue.

clue.text: Cooked lamb, say, will be awful

indicators.note: cooked food is altered by preparation, as these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that badly prepared lamb will taste dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges the letters of LAMB and SAY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal means extremely bad, a strong synonym of awful.

clue.text: View offered by soldiers in Hispanic republic

indicators.note: the soldiers sit inside the republic's name

parts.note: Panama is a Spanish-speaking Central American republic
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A scenic vista offered by troops stationed in a Latin American country.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, unbroken view of a surrounding area.

clue.text: Looters stumble on the way up, drinking beer

indicators.note: the reversed word takes the beer inside it, as a drinker does
in a down clue going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: to slip is to lose footing, a stumble
lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Drunken raiders tripping as they climb, still swigging beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' works because this is a down clue, so the stumble word is read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillagers are plunderers who loot property, usually in war.

clue.text: Upset, cancelled dispatch, ignoring son

parts.note: an event that is off has been called off

indicators.note: ignoring the son means leaving his letter out

parts.note: to send is to dispatch

explanation.surface: Annoyed that a shipment was called off, with the son overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' removes S from SEND to leave END.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend is to hurt someone's feelings, so it means to upset as a verb.

clue.text: Company staff needed to do auctions on behalf of church

parts.note: auctions are sales of goods to the highest bidder
acting for someone is acting on their behalf
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Employees required to run auctions for the church.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the Church of England, the established church in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales force is the team of a company's employees who sell its products.

clue.text: Understand origin of revolutionary straw material

parts.note: to see is to understand, as in I see

indicators.note: the origin of the word is its first letter

parts.note: a sucker is someone easily fooled, a straw man or easy dupe

explanation.surface: Grasping where a revolutionary drinking straw came from.
explanation.walkthrough: SUCKER here is taken as a drinking straw, something you suck through.
explanation.definitionFit: Seersucker is a puckered cotton fabric, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: Ox boxed in by prize bull

indicators.note: the letters are enclosed within the words prize bull

explanation.surface: A cow penned in alongside a prize-winning bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxed in by' finds the letters inside 'priZE BUll'.
explanation.definitionFit: A zebu is a humped domestic ox of India and Africa.

clue.text: Drake, for example, taking 50 from River Plate, perversely

indicators.note: perversely means in a twisted way, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Sir Francis Drake seizing fifty ships from the River Plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking 50 from' removes L from the letters of RIVER PLATE, and 'perversely' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Drake was a privateer, a sea captain licensed by the Crown to raid enemy ships.

clue.text: Withdrew accountant involved in new tender

indicators.note: the accountant is caught up inside the other letters
new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An accountant took back a fresh bid for a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' reads as a bid for a contract, but it is only the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to take back a statement or belief formally.

clue.text: Bureaucrat will be protected by them — and a ringleader

indicators.note: the answer's letters sit sheltered inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A civil servant who will be guarded by a gang and its boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be protected by' finds the letters spanning 'theM — AND A RINgleader'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a powerful senior civil servant, originally a Chinese official.

clue.text: Goodbyes as sexy regularly producing such a journey

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Farewells as seductive as these lead to a long voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'gOoDbYeS aS sExY'.
explanation.definitionFit: An odyssey is a long, eventful journey, named after Odysseus's wandering voyage home.

clue.text: Nudes frolicking in a river — separately

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the other pieces
frolicking means playing about, so the letters skip about

explanation.surface: Naked bathers splashing about in a river, apart from each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frolicking' rearranges NUDES to SUNDE, which goes 'in' A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunder means apart or into separate pieces.

clue.text: Former morning paper

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A newspaper that used to come out in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'morning paper' looks like a newspaper, but paper here is a test sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: An examination paper is the set of questions in a test.

clue.text: Makers of shorts may be quiet during bumpy rides

indicators.note: the quiet word is placed in the middle of the other letters
a bumpy ride throws things about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: still means silent or calm

explanation.surface: Clothes makers might keep silent on rough journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shorts' suggests trousers, but here it means small measures of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorts are measures of spirits such as whisky, which distillers produce.

clue.text: Sudden influx of popular crowd having missed the start

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the first letter of the crowd word is dropped

parts.note: a crush is a dense crowd of people

explanation.surface: A flood of fans into a popular venue, arriving late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having missed the start' removes C from CRUSH to leave RUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: An inrush is a sudden flowing or crowding in, much like an influx.

clue.text: Nation occupying borders of huge sandy bay

indicators.note: what occupies the borders of a word is everything inside its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A country stretching along the edge of a vast sandy bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying borders of' takes the insides of hUGe, sANDy and bAy.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda is a landlocked country in East Africa, so it is a nation.

clue.text: Various items from right-wingers on newspaper

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
dries were hardline Thatcherite Conservatives, opposed to the wets

explanation.surface: Assorted goods from Conservatives writing for a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid; DRIES were hardline right-wing Tories under Margaret Thatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundries are miscellaneous small items too minor to list separately.

clue.text: Bird causing Hemingway perhaps to lose way

indicators.note: losing means dropping these letters from the name

parts.note: Ernest Hemingway, the American novelist
ST is an abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A bird that makes a famous author go astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' takes ST from ERNEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a crossword favourite among birds.

clue.text: Sports people streak excitedly across at last

indicators.note: an excited state stirs things up, so the letters are mixed
at last points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Athletes finally dash across in great excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' rearranges STREAK; 'at last' takes the S that ends 'across'.
explanation.definitionFit: Skaters take part in sports such as figure skating or speed skating.

clue.text: Service odds good after performing?

indicators.note: the good letter comes after the performing word

parts.note: evens is a betting price, odds of one to one
on means on stage, performing

explanation.surface: A betting tip on a church service going well once it is under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places G behind ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening prayer service of the Anglican Church.

clue.text: Weapon's journey north in case of target

indicators.note: the journey and north pieces go inside the outer letters
the case of a word is its outside letters, its first and last

parts.note: a ride is a journey on horseback or by vehicle

explanation.surface: A weapon travels north inside a protective case towards its target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in case of' puts RIDE and N inside T...T, the first and last letters of 'target'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, so it is a weapon.
